Definition: A unique identifier for the media file. Concatenating collectionID and fileName is considered best practice.
The name of the media file. Prefixing still images with "IMG" and and moving images with "MOV" is considered best practice.
A unique identifier for the collection. Using a stable Digital Object Identifier is considered best practice.
The name of the collection.
Example(s): Eileen Graham's Collection, Discovery Bay, Jamaica, (1966–1968).

Definition: The nature of the resource. Constraints: StillImage, MovingImage.
A bibliographic reference for the resource.
Example(s): Johnson, K. and Jones, L.A. (2026) Eileen Graham Collection, Discovery Bay, Jamaica (1966–1968). https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22663465.

Definition: A legal document giving official permission to do something with the resource.
A person or organisation owning or managing rights over the resource.
Example(s): Trustees of the Natural History Museum

Definition: Name or identifier of the person or organization that captured the media.
Name or identifier of the person or organization that digitized the media.
Name or identifier of the person or organization that processed the media.
The four-digit year in which the media was captured, according to the Common Era Calendar.
The integer month in which the media was captured.
The integer day of the month in which the media was captured.
A category or description of the habitat in which the media was captured.
Example(s): reef flat, reef edge, reef slope

Definition: The name of the water body in which the media was captured. Using a standard gazetters is considered best practice (e.g. marineregions.org).
The name of the island group in which the media was captured. Using a standard gazetters is considered best practice (e.g. marineregions.org).
The name of the island in which the media was captured. Using a standard gazetters is considered best practice (e.g. marineregions.org).
The name of the country or major administrative unit in which the media was captured.
The standard code for the country in which the media was captured (ISO 3166-1-alpha-2).
The name of the next smaller administrative region than country (state, province, canton, department, region, etc.) in which the media was captured.
The full, unabbreviated name of the next smaller administrative region than stateProvince (county, shire, department, etc.) in which the media was captured.
The full, unabbreviated name of the next smaller administrative region than county (city, municipality, etc.) in which the media was captured.
The specific description of the place.
A geographic longitude (in decimal degrees) as per EPSG:4326 geodetic datum. Always reported in Eastings.
A geographic latitude (in decimal degrees) as per EPSG:4326 geodetic datum. Always reported in Northings.
Comments or notes about the spatial description determination, explaining assumptions made or the protocol.
Example(s): Coordinates inferred from local feature (buoy), precise to the nearest minute (0.01).

Definition: The least depth within a range of depths in metres.
The greatest depth within a range of depths in metres.
Any comments or notes about the media file.
Date on which the resource was changed. Formatted as an ISO 8601 string (YYYY-MM-DD).
A unique identifier of the observation.
A unique identifier for the media.
The type of the observation.
The value of the observation.
An identifier or uniform resource locator (URL) that points to further context related to the observation value (e.g. scientific name ID).
Horizontal position of the top-left corner of a bounding box that encompasses the observed individual(s) in the media file identified by mediaID.
Vertical position of the top-left corner of a bounding box that encompasses the observed individual(s) in the media file identified by mediaID.
Width of a bounding box that encompasses the observed individual(s) in the media file identified by mediaID.
Height of the bounding box that encompasses the observed individual(s) in the media file identified by mediaID.
Method used to classify the observation. Constraints: Human, Machine.
Name or identifier of the person or AI algorithm that classified the observation.
Date and time of the classification. Formatted as an ISO 8601 string with timezone designator (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ).
Degree of certainty of the classification. Expressed as a probability, with 1 being maximum certainty.
Comments or notes about the observation.
Example(s): Training dataset for project fish count
